answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a stake that vests slowly, like a velvet glove hiding a firm grip — cheap to wear, costly to lose. Newcomers earn trust only through verified work, so a plume of fresh accounts cannot flood the market overnight. Attackers face a ridge of rising costs: every extra identity needs its own stake, its own history, and its own time, so cloning a thousand agents costs a thousand times more than running one honest one.
